findings.reason: an operator reading that receipt sees the disposition it just recorded reported as open, and this codebase's own rule is that a receipt must report what a later read reports; the done-when should require the receipt to name the figure disposition, as it already does for the store read-back, or it will land a command whose answer looks unrecorded.
findings.text: §24's done-when proves the disposition landed by reading the store back, but the command's own receipt is composed from a record that takes no rubric, so `crew dispose --rubric figure` writes the answer onto the figure record but its `disposition` field is rendered from the run's text record and reports the figure finding as unanswered (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:718-760`: the receipt reads a text-only record, and `review_dispositions.stored_record_for_disposition` at :321 has no `rubric` parameter). The write path already covers `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`, so the node can fix it, but the measure does not ask for it.

findings.reason: §18 and §19 both model a figure review as coexisting with a text review of the same head, so the text record the guard requires is present whenever §20 folds the figure record in; the gap is a boundary the plan's own model excludes, and widening it would creep the node onto an unreferenced code path without changing §23's deliverable.
findings.text: §23 says the fix swaps in the merged review once "where `dispatch_repair_for_run` reads the stored review", naming a single merge point, but the function also reads the text-only record at `reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:649` (`review_module.stored_record(project, run_id)`, no rubric) as a presence guard before its first finding check. A run whose only stored record is a figure review returns "no review is stored for this run" there and never reaches the merge, so the sentence's claim that "every later read in the function" sees the figure findings is true only for a run that already carries a text record.
